quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Reduce speed and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Why should you use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop?

options.text: Using only one brake will wear them unevenly.
It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
Using both brakes is the only way to slow a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes during normal stops builds a habit of always using both. This habit is important in emergencies, when using both brakes may save your life.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
A motorcycle is easier to see than a car.
You should pass on the shoulder, not the main road.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars. Other drivers may not notice you, or you may disappear into their blind spot. Always assume they cannot see you.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees they will yield to you.
Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
Means they know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means another driver will yield to you. Drivers can look directly at you and still not see you.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good way to increase your visibility?

options.text: Using your headlight all the time

questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection quickly.
Speed up so others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look at motorcycles but still do not notice them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: When choosing clothes for riding, which is NOT a good choice?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: For protection, wear a DOT-compliant helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high ankle-covering boots or shoes, and durable gloves.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should NOT:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently if you need to brake.

questions.question: Which provides the best face protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time to stop quickly. Press down firmly. Do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Use the brake on the tire that is flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly use the brake on the tire that is not flat (if you are sure which one it is).

questions.question: Where should you get your main information about your motorcycle?

options.text: From a library book about motorcycles.

questions.explanation: The owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. Read the manual before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help you avoid serious injury?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a jacket and long pants made of sturdy material, high and sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves. Ear buds do not provide protection.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding. The wobble will likely stop on its own.
Close the throttle to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up. Instead, grip the handlebars tightly, slow down by closing the throttle gradually, lean your weight forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as you can. Once off the road, fix the problem causing the wobble.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: On only one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Place loads as low as possible. Putting them too high, like on a sissy bar, raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and affects balance. Spread loads evenly on both sides of the motorcycle to keep it balanced.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a result of long-term cold weather riding?
questions.explanation: Riding in cold weather for long periods can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from cold weather.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, how should they pass?

options.text: In a staggered formation with several riders passing at once.

questions.explanation: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. One rider must finish passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: More often than you look ahead.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to stay aware of what is behind you and spot potential hazards.

questions.question: For a face shield to work well, it should NOT:

options.text: Allow clear views to both sides.

questions.explanation: A good face shield should be free of scratches, resist breaking, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, and allow air to flow through. A completely sealed face shield will fog up and make it hard to see.
